items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I turned to Billy Mitchell and I said, “Mr. Mitchell, thank you very much for letting me sit in with you. It was an honor.”

ctx.x: Somebody asked him, they said, “I’d like to take a lesson with you in improvisation.” And Chet, who is a little salty sometimes, said, “well improvisation is about imagination or lack of it.” So I always remembered that. You’d better have something to say, otherwise don’t say much. Say a little then get out. A long, long time ago I went to a jam session at a club in Seaford, Long Island called Sonny’s Place. It was a club that was there for many years and many great players and singers stopped in there just to…

another one.” I said, “yes indeed.” So to be accepted by somebody who I looked up to, I wouldn’t have cared if he threw me off the bandstand. Because that’s what they do. But to be accepted like that is like just huge for me. I mean I drove home, it was like a two hour drive home, I’m going like, “wow, Billy Mitchell said it was okay.” And then I got a gig, about three months later. He [Sonny] gave me a date that night, for three months down the road. And I showed up with a rhythm section with guys that I knew…

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Like Billy Mitchell. I got to sit in at a gig, and I don’t know if we talked about this. Yeah I mean Billy Mitchell, “Yeah come by and sit in.” Billy Mitchell is running the band.

ctx.x: But I wonder if your attitude about the music would have been different.

I wouldn’t have known half of the stuff that I found out the best way, from experience. The experience is the best teacher. The tuition is very high. Yeah. But it’s worth it ‘cause if they pluck you out of a music school, you might know how to play or execute, and then they make you leader. Well you don’t even know how to be a sideman. How can you be a leader if you’ve never been a sideman? And if you’ve never worked for a good leader and a bad leader, how do you know what it is to be a good leader? If you’ve…

Well how the heck does a student these days learn that protocol? You had sort of mentioned that in today’s jazz education it seems that there are some people are now teaching who weren’t able to participate in that learning process. So you have mostly book-schooled professors now teaching another generation.
